message.reasoning:
We need to produce a test class for BaseJsonValidator.getSchemaNode(). Since BaseJsonValidator is abstract, we need a concrete subclass for testing. Could create an anonymous subclass via extending BaseJsonValidator with minimal implementation of abstract methods (validate). The method getSchemaNode just returns the field schemaNode set in constructor. So test that constructor correctly assigns schemaNode and getter returns same reference.

We need to set up dependencies: JsonSchema parentSchema, ValidatorTypeCode validatorType, ValidationContext validationContext, schemaNode (JsonNode), schemaPath string. Use Mockito to mock these dependencies, as they are complex.

We need to import Jackson JsonNode, maybe use ObjectMapper to create a JsonNode.

We'll create a concrete class TestValidator extends BaseJsonValidator with dummy validate method returning empty set.

In setupBeforeEach, create mocks for parentSchema, validatorType, validationContext; also create a JsonNode using ObjectMapper.readTree("{\"type\":\"string\"}").

Construct the validator: new TestValidator("testPath", schemaNode, parentSchema, validatorType, validationContext, false);

Then test getSchemaNode returns same object.

Also test that if schemaNode is null, getter returns null.

Potentially also test that schemaNode can be changed (field is protected, but we shouldn't set directly). We can use reflection to set field for second test, but requirement: not to invoke private methods or fields of target class and dependent class. Changing protected field via subclass maybe allowed? But we can just construct with null.

So two test methods.

Add necessary imports: java.util.Set, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode, java.util.Collections, java.util.HashSet, etc.

Implement validate method returning empty set.

Make sure to annotate test methods with @Test.

Now produce final code in markdown.
